questions.stem: A 71-year-old woman presented with fevers and a discharging wound on her right calf. She had a recent right calf fasciotomy due to a popliteal thrombus and end-stage renal disease on regular thrice-weekly conventional hemodialysis. She had no known drug allergies. On examination her temperature was 38.6°C, and there was purulent discharge from her right calf incision site. Investigations: Total white blood cell count 12,500 cells/mm3 Wound swab culture: positive for methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) 2/2 blood cultures positive for MSSA
questions.lead_in: What would be most appropriate for thrice-weekly posthemodialysis dosing for treatment of this patient’s infection, assuming a planned duration of therapy of 4–6 weeks?
questions.explanation: Cefazolin Ceftazidime is only marginally active against MSSA and would not be appropriate. Linezolid dosing is unaffected by renal insufficiency or dialysis and should not be given just postdialysis. Oritavancin is not established for treatment of MSSA bacteremia nor for treatment courses of 4–6 weeks in length. Vancomycin has been found to be clinically inferior to beta-lactams (including cefazolin) for MSSA infection in patients with end-stage renal diseases on regular thriceweekly hemodialysis. Cefazolin postdialysis dosing has been shown to be effective for MSSA bacteremia in patients with end-stage renal disease.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 8 Q2

questions.question: Resistance of antibiotics.

parts.text: Resistant to imipenem and meropenem but sensitive to piperacillin and ceftazidime. What is the mechanism of resistance?
Resistant to amp, cefazolin, and cefox but Intermediate to Ceftriaxone. What is the mechanism of resistance?

questions.model_answer: a) Pseudomonas-type organism resistant to imipenem/meropenem but sensitive to piperacillin/ceftazidime: loss/downregulation of the OprD porin channel (selective carbapenem-specific entry porin), which does not affect piperacillin or ceftazidime entry; efflux pump overexpression (e.g. MexAB-OprM) is an alternative/additional contributing mechanism. b) E. coli resistant to ampicillin, cefazolin, cefoxitin, intermediate to ceftriaxone: plasmid-mediated AmpC β-lactamase (e.g. CMY-type), which hydrolyzes penicillins and cephamycins (cefoxitin) and reduces susceptibility to extended-spectrum cephalosporins.
questions.beyond_mandell: Mechanisms consistent with Mandell Ch. Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterobacteriaceae resistance chapters

questions.question: For the following antibiotics, describe their i) capacity for inducing AmpC (strong/weak), ii) susceptibility to hydrolysis by AmpC (high/low), iii) whether they are recommended for invasive infection.

parts.text: Ceftriaxone
Cefepime
Piperacillin-tazobactam
Ceftazidime-avibactam
Imipenem

questions.model_answer:
Ceftriaxone: weak AmpC inducer; HIGH susceptibility to AmpC hydrolysis; NOT recommended for invasive infection with an AmpC-producing organism.
Cefepime: weak AmpC inducer; LOW susceptibility to AmpC hydrolysis (relatively stable); may be considered/recommended for invasive infection with an AmpC producer.
Piperacillin-tazobactam: weak-to-moderate inducer; HIGH susceptibility to hydrolysis (tazobactam does not reliably inhibit AmpC); NOT recommended for invasive infection with an AmpC producer.
Ceftazidime-avibactam: avibactam inhibits AmpC, so LOW susceptibility to hydrolysis; recommended for invasive infection with an AmpC producer.
Imipenem: strong AmpC inducer, but LOW susceptibility to hydrolysis (carbapenems are stable against AmpC); recommended for invasive infection, including with stably derepressed AmpC producers.
questions.beyond_mandell: Clinical treatment recommendations for AmpC-producing Enterobacterales reflect current IDSA guidance on resistant gram-negative infections.

parts.text: Cefiderocol - What are the two components of this drug and what is the antibacterial mechanism of both?

questions.model_answer: Cefiderocol has two components: (1) a cephalosporin core (structurally related to ceftazidime/cefepime) that binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits bacterial cell wall (peptidoglycan) transpeptidation, the standard beta-lactam mechanism (2) a catechol-type siderophore side chain that chelates free iron; this iron-drug complex is actively transported across the bacterial outer membrane via TonB-dependent iron-transport systems ('Trojan horse' mechanism), greatly enhancing periplasmic penetration, particularly in multidrug-resistant gram-negative organisms.

parts.text: 2 different components and their mechanism

cohort_answer.text: Cefiderocol (catechol-cephalosporin): Catechol side chain chelates ferric iron and is actively transported into the bacterial cell through the outer cell membrane via a bacterial iron transporter whose chief function is delivering iron nutrients to the cell wall. Cephalosporin component binds to peptidoglycan proteins (PBP-3, seen among non-fermenters), inhibiting the final stage of transpeptidation of peptidoglycan synthesis in the cell wall, inhibiting cell wall synthesis. No gram positive or anaerobic activity (similar spectrum to Ceftazidime). Dosed 2-3g every 8 hours as extended infusion, needs CrCl adjustment. Cephalosporin component has high affinity for PBP3 (structurally similar to Cefepime, pyrrolidin group on C3 side chain, greater stability against beta-lactamases); carboxy-propanoxyomino group on C7 improves transport across outer membrane. Siderophore component: chlorocatechol group at end of C3 confers siderophore activity, an iron transporter allowing transport through transporters ('Iron Trojan Horse') avoiding resistance mechanisms such as porins and efflux pumps.

parts.text: a) What is the antimicrobial coverage?
b) What side effect is specific to cefepime?
c) What would make you recommend adding this to your hospital's formulary?

cohort_answer.text: a) Gram positives incl MSSA, S. pneumo, EXCEPT MRSA/Enterococcus. Gram negatives incl Enterobacteriaceae (stable AmpC activity), Pseudomonas, sometimes Acinetobacter, EXCEPT Steno, B. cepacia. Anaerobes: some activity vs GP anaerobes, inactive vs GN anaerobes (incl B. fragilis). No atypical coverage. b) Severe neurological reactions: encephalopathy, aphasia, myoclonus, seizures, non-convulsive status epilepticus; attributed to crossing BBB and concentration-dependent GABA antagonism; predominantly in critically ill/renal impairment patients. c) Broadest spectrum cephalosporin with enhanced activity against Enterobacteriaceae incl AmpC beta-lactamases and Pseudomonas; important for MDR gram negative nosocomial infections; high intrinsic potency from rapid periplasmic space penetration.

parts.text: Patient is allergic to ceftriaxone with anaphylaxis, name two options with dose and route.
Resistant to cefixime but sensitive to ceftriaxone – what is the mechanism of resistance.

cohort_answer.text: Two options: Azithro 2g po x1 dose + gentamicin 240mg IM x1 dose; Doxy 100mg bid po x7 days + gentamicin 240mg IM x1 dose; Azithromycin 2g po x1 dose + cipro 500mg po x1 dose. Mechanism of resistance: Point mutation on PBP2a for cefixime, multiple mutations for ceftriaxone resistance; Efflux (mtr gene), beta lactamase (TEM)

questions.question: Staph aureus with cefoxitin disk R.

parts.text: To what drug does this predict resistance?
What is the most likely gene involved and gene product causing resistance? Explain mode of resistance.

cohort_answer.text: Predicts resistance to: Methicillin resistance - oxacillin, cefazolin, cephalexin. Gene: mecA gene - encodes PBP2a that has a low affinity for beta lactam abx. Mode of resistance: Target site alteration

questions.question: Name the molecular target of each antifungal drug in the table.

parts.text: Posaconazole
Micafungin
Amphotericin
Terbinafine

questions.model_answer:
Posaconazole: lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (fungal CYP51), blocking ergosterol synthesis.
Micafungin: (1,3)-beta-D-glucan synthase, blocking fungal cell wall glucan synthesis.
Amphotericin B: binds ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane, forming pores that disrupt membrane integrity.
Terbinafine: squalene epoxidase, blocking an earlier step of ergosterol synthesis.

parts.text: Name 3 mechanisms of resistance possessed by P. aeruginosa that this antibiotic bypasses

cohort_answer.text: Efflux pumps (MexAB-OprD); Porin mutations (OprD); Modification of PBPs (ceftolozane potent inhibitor of PBP1b and 3); overexpression of AmpC (affinity for PBP4 not significant enough to induce AmpC); Class A and C beta-lactamases (tazobactam inhibits). Not effective against MBL, KPC, or OXA-48 carbapenemases

parts.text: Name three mechanisms of resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa that would still render the isolate susceptible to ceftolazane/tazobactam.

questions.model_answer: Mechanisms of Pseudomonas resistance that still leave the isolate susceptible to ceftolozane-tazobactam (3): (1) Loss of OprD porin (carbapenem resistance without affecting ceftolozane entry). (2) Efflux pump overexpression (e.g. MexAB-OprM, MexXY) - ceftolozane is a poor substrate for these pumps. (3) AmpC overproduction/derepression - ceftolozane is stable to AmpC hydrolysis even when overexpressed, unlike other cephalosporins.

questions.question: List of paired antimicrobials (14 pairs) asked which you would choose for. (3 - 0.5 each); Valganciclovir over acyclovir; Famciclovir over acyclovir; Doxycycline over Septra; Metronidazole over clindamycin; Piptazo over meropenem; Ampicillin over cloxacillin; cefazolin over cloxacillin; Cefuroxime over CTX; Moxifloxacin over levofloxacin; Fluconazole over caspofungin; Atovaquone over dapsone

parts.text: I would pick _____ over _____ because patient on carbamazepine
I would pick _____ over _____ because patient has G6PD deficiency
I would pick _____ over _____ because drug NOT used for C.diff treatment and NOT associated with development of C.diff
I would pick _____ over _____ because it has superior renal penetration
I would pick _____ over _____ because it works better for CMV
I would pick _____ over _____ because I need CNS coverage

questions.model_answer:
a) Because patient is on carbamazepine (a potent CYP3A4 inducer with significant drug-interaction potential with azoles): choose caspofungin over fluconazole to avoid a clinically significant CYP-mediated interaction.
b) Because patient has G6PD deficiency: choose atovaquone over dapsone (dapsone causes oxidative hemolysis in G6PD deficiency; atovaquone does not).
c) Because the drug is NOT used for C. difficile treatment and NOT associated with causing C. difficile: choose doxycycline over Septra (TMP-SMX) - doxycycline carries a low risk of precipitating C. difficile infection and is not a CDI treatment.
d) Because of superior renal/urinary penetration: choose cefazolin over cloxacillin (cefazolin achieves higher urinary concentrations; cloxacillin has substantial hepatobiliary elimination).
e) Because it works better for CMV: choose valganciclovir over acyclovir (acyclovir has minimal activity against CMV; valganciclovir/ganciclovir are the drugs of choice).
f) Because CNS coverage is needed: choose moxifloxacin over levofloxacin (moxifloxacin achieves higher CNS penetration due to greater lipophilicity).
questions.beyond_mandell: Drug-interaction and PK comparative reasoning drawn from general pharmacology, not this Mandell chapter specifically.

parts.text: Name the 3 species from the Enterobacterales family that has the highest risk of clinically important ampC production

For each of the following, indicate if it is a strong or weak inducer of ampC (strong/weak), risk for hydrolysis by ampC (high/low), and if it is recommended for invasive infections (yes/no): Ceftriaxone, Cefepime, Pip-Tazo, Ceftaz-Avi, Imipenem

cohort_answer.text: 3 species: Enterobacter cloacae; Citrobacter freundii; Klebsiella aerogenes. Table - Ceftriaxone: Weak inducer, High hydrolysis risk, Not recommended. Cefepime: Weak inducer, Low hydrolysis risk (MIC<2), Recommended (MIC<4). Tazocin: Weak inducer, High hydrolysis risk, Not recommended. Ceftaz-Avi: Weak inducer, Low hydrolysis risk, Not recommended (limited data, for complicated UTI/intra-abdominal infections only). Imipenem: Strong inducer, Low hydrolysis risk, Recommended

questions.question: 22. What are three mechanisms of resistance in Pseudomonas that would render an isolate still susceptible to ceftolozane-tazobactam? (3)

parts.text: What are three mechanisms of resistance in Pseudomonas that would render an isolate still susceptible to ceftolozane-tazobactam? (3)

cohort_answer.text: Unaffected by porin channels (Mandell); unaffected by upregulation of efflux pumps (Mandell); MexXY efflux system (exports fluoroquinolones, tetracyclines, aminoglycosides, and anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam agents); Enzymes: TEM-1, SHV-1, CTX-M, AmpC or ESBL (chromosomal beta lactamases); Aminoglycoside modifying enzymes (reduce susceptibility to all AG).
